q2_gaps: impersonal generic "one" as subject — the pronoun rule sends a pronoun with no antecedent to a fresh witness classed `person`, and the generic-signal rule requires a bare plural or an explicit quantifier, so nothing licenses reading "one" as a kind-level generic even though that is what the sentence means

colon apposition spelling out a cataphoric quantified NP ("for only one thing: in order to win"), where the purpose clause after the colon is the content of "one thing" and the for-PP is not separately realised
a focus particle scoping over a purpose adjunct rather than over a clause participant or the VP — the filler rule names subject, object and VP-lemma cases only
notes: Folding the focus and connective atoms into the rule's consequent makes them inherit the rule's (STV 0.9 0.9), whereas the instruction set fixes focus atoms and connective atoms at (STV 1.0 0.99); the rule form leaves no way to give them their own truth value.
